title: Majority vote over sampled answers
description: The simplest consensus: sample N completions from one or more models and take the most common answer. Self-consistency (Wang et al.) showed this reliably beats single-shot generation on reasoning tasks because independent reasoning paths converge on correct answers more often than on any single wrong one.
method: Sample N reasoning chains at temperature > 0, normalize answers (strip whitespace, canonicalize numbers), and select the mode; ties break by highest mean token log-probability.
usage: Wrap any QA call: sample 10 answers, vote, and return the winner with its vote share as a confidence signal.

demo.code:
from collections import Counter
answers = ['42', '42', '41', '42', '43', '42']
winner, votes = Counter(answers).most_common(1)[0]
print(f'consensus: {winner} ({votes}/{len(answers)} votes)')

title: LLM-as-judge scoring panel
description: Instead of voting on identical outputs, a judge model scores candidate answers against a rubric (correctness, completeness, clarity). Panels of judges — or one judge with a strict rubric — pick winners in generation tournaments, RLHF data curation, and eval harnesses like MT-Bench.
method: Candidates are presented pairwise or listwise to the judge with a scoring rubric; judges output scores plus rationales; the top scorer wins, with position-bias mitigation by swapping candidate order.
usage: Define the rubric first, run each candidate through the judge twice (orders swapped), and average.

demo.code:
cands = {'A': 8.5, 'B': 7.0, 'C': 9.0}
winner = max(cands, key=cands.get)
print('judge scores:', cands)
print('winner:', winner, '-> selected for output')

title: Condorcet pairwise ranking
description: When models rank multiple candidate answers, Condorcet voting compares every pair head-to-head: the candidate beating all others pairwise wins. It avoids vote-splitting pathologies of simple plurality when several similar good answers divide the vote.
method: Each agent submits a ranking; build the pairwise matrix (how many agents prefer X over Y); the Condorcet winner beats every rival; fall back to ranked-pairs if a cycle appears.
usage: Use when choosing among several plausible outputs (summaries, designs); collect rankings, compute the matrix, declare the winner.

demo.code:
import itertools
rankings = [['A','B','C'], ['A','C','B'], ['B','A','C']]
cands = ['A','B','C']
for x, y in itertools.combinations(cands, 2):
    xy = sum(1 for r in rankings if r.index(x) < r.index(y))
    print(f'{x} over {y}: {xy}-{len(rankings)-xy}')
print('A beats B 2-1 and C 3-0 -> Condorcet winner: A')

title: Delphi-method iterative polling
description: The Delphi method, from 1950s RAND forecasting, polls experts anonymously in rounds, sharing anonymized summaries between rounds until opinions converge. With LLMs as the experts, it removes dominant-voice bias: no agent knows who said what, so convergence comes from reasons, not reputations.
method: Round r: each agent answers privately with reasons. Facilitator summarizes positions and key arguments anonymously. Round r+1: agents revise. Stop when variance drops below threshold or rounds exhaust.
usage: Best for forecasts and estimates: 3-5 rounds, numeric answers with reasons, track convergence.

demo.code:
est = [2030, 2028, 2035, 2031]
print('round 1 estimates:', est, 'spread:', max(est) - min(est))
est2 = [2030, 2030, 2032, 2031]
print('round 2 estimates:', est2, 'spread:', max(est2) - min(est2), '-> converged')

title: Stacked generalization of model outputs
description: Stacking trains a meta-model on the outputs of base models: each base LLM answers, and a small classifier or regressor learns which model to trust for which inputs. Unlike fixed weights, the meta-learner adapts trust by input features — model A for math, model B for prose.
method: Collect base-model answers on a labeled set; featurize (task type, answer length, model confidences); train the meta-model; at inference, base models run in parallel and the meta-model picks or blends.
usage: Build the labeled set from past judgments; retrain the meta-model as base models change.

demo.code:
print('stacking decision table:')
table = [('math', 'trust model A (0.94 math acc)'), ('prose', 'trust model B (0.91 prose acc)')]
for task, rule in table:
    print(f'  {task:6} -> {rule}')
print('meta-model routes per input features.')

title: CRDT merge of partial agent drafts
description: When agents draft different sections of one document, conflict-free replicated data types (CRDTs) merge their edits without a central arbiter. Each agent works on its own replica; the merge is associative, commutative, and idempotent — order of arrival never changes the result.
method: Represent the draft as a CRDT (e.g., Yjs/YATA for text, OR-Set for lists); agents apply local ops; replicas sync and merge deterministically; final document is the join of all ops.
usage: Give each agent a replica of the shared doc, let them edit concurrently, and sync on a timer or on demand.

title: Byzantine-tolerant agent quorum
description: Borrowed from distributed systems: with up to f malicious or faulty agents, 3f+1 agents and 2f+1 agreeing votes guarantee a correct decision. Applied to LLM teams, it bounds how many hallucinating or compromised agents the consensus can survive — relevant when agents come from untrusted sources.
method: Agents commit to answers (hash reveal), then reveal; a decision needs 2f+1 matching reveals; equivocating agents are slashed from the pool.
usage: Use when agents are untrusted or independently operated; keep f small (1-2) since cost scales with n.

demo.code:
agents = ['A-ok', 'B-ok', 'C-byzantine', 'D-ok']
votes = ['yes', 'yes', 'no', 'yes']
print('agents:', agents)
print('2f+1 quorum with f=1 needs 3 matching ->', 'yes' if votes.count('yes') >= 3 else 'no')

title: Weighted voting by model calibration
description: Not all models are equal: weighted voting gives each model's ballot a weight from its historical accuracy or calibration score on similar tasks. A small accurate specialist can outvote two mediocre generalists, which plain majority vote cannot express.
method: Maintain per-model, per-task-type accuracy from past judgments; weight = log(accuracy/(1-accuracy)) (log-odds); the answer with the highest summed weight wins.
usage: Log every model's verdicts with ground truth when available; recompute weights nightly; apply at consensus time.

demo.code:
votes = [('A', 'yes', 0.9), ('B', 'no', 0.7), ('C', 'no', 0.6)]
import math
score = {}
for m, v, acc in votes:
    w = math.log(acc / (1 - acc))
    score[v] = score.get(v, 0) + w
print('weighted scores:', {k: round(x, 2) for k, x in score.items()})
print('winner:', max(score, key=score.get))
